assembly: Seat the rear frame in the base, insert both frame-retaining keys through the aligned tenon passages, then slide both braces to their dovetail stops and verify the frame is square.
Insert the central dead axle from the rear so its flange seats in the frame recess.

Slide the lunar slider into the carrier dovetail from the open spoke tip. From the rear, pass the follower axle through the roller, carrier radial slot, and slider D-bore, leaving its front retention tip exposed.

Place the roller inside the fixed cam race while lowering the carrier over the dead axle; rotate the moon 20 degrees onto the follower-axle lugs so it retains the axle and verify both positive lug stops.
Install the retaining washer and transverse key, then verify the carrier rotates without rubbing and stays within the declared endplay target.
Slide the stationary central eye guard over the fixed axle D-tip, confirming its rear face clears the rotating carrier and its relief channel leaves the retention key serviceable.
Slide the hollow 20T pinion/spindle from the front over the fixed frame post and mesh it with the 40T gear at the nominal 37.5 mm center distance.
Key the crank arm onto the rotating D-sleeve, then fit the pinion-post washer and stationary retaining key and verify 0.3-0.5 mm axial endplay.
Slide the crank grip over its arm post and install the grip washer and tapered key, preserving 0.4 mm grip endplay.
Install both static lips into their keyed sockets, maintaining the declared depth overlap and 6 mm exposed clearance.
Turn the crank slowly through two turns and inspect full follower capture, slider travel, gear mesh, axial separation, and lip clearance before normal operation.
assumptions: A typical 200 x 200 mm FDM bed can accommodate the 190 x 70 mm base and the 188 x 176 mm rear frame when placed individually, subject to slicer skirt/brim margins.
The declared 0.30 mm-per-side dovetail clearance, 0.35 mm nominal shaft clearance, and 0.4 mm roller end clearance are starting values to be parameterized, not universal printer facts.
PLA or PETG can be used, but material-dependent friction, creep, keyed retention, and layer adhesion are not established here.
The 2:1 reduction is intended to make the 286-degree inner orbit readable and keep hand force modest; required torque is not yet measured.
The object is operated upright on its base and held at the base rather than by the lips, moon, or crank.
concept.category: Hand-cranked desktop kinetic automaton; no electronics, loose payload, adhesive, or purchased hardware.
concept.claims_boundary: No claim is made here for a successful print, physical fit, safe age grade, measured torque, cycle life, wear life, durability, or human delight. CAD checks and simulation in Make may support geometry and motion but will not substitute for physical evidence.

coordinate_and_layer_authority.clear_layering_decision: The crank, lips, moon, carrier, cam, and rear frame occupy distinct depth bands so projected paths may overlap without physical interference. Make must preserve these bands or re-prove all clearances.
coordinate_and_layer_authority.depth: Depth positions are measured front-to-rear. Crank grip occupies 0-28 mm, crank arm and pinion shield 28-34 mm, lip plates 33-36 mm in their non-overlapping upper-right region, central eye disc 36.5-39.5 mm with its hub ending at 47.0 mm, moon 37-47 mm outside the eye radius, slider/carrier/gears 47.5-52.5 mm, follower/cam 53-59.5 mm, and rear frame 59.5-63.5 mm; the 70 mm base contains the entire stack.
coordinate_and_layer_authority.front_view: Origin is the orbit center; +x points right and +y points up. Carrier angle is clockwise from 12 o'clock.

cycle.drive_ratio: A 20-tooth pinion drives a 40-tooth carrier gear, so two counterclockwise crank turns produce one clockwise lunar cycle.
cycle.load_path: Hand to rotating grip, grip post to crank arm, D-shaft to 20T pinion, pinion to 40T carrier, carrier dovetail to lunar slider, follower roller to fixed cam race, then rear frame, braces, and base.

phases.moon_center_motion: Retract from radius 70 mm to 58 mm behind the lower static lip using a cosine-eased cam transition.
Hold radius 58 mm for 286 degrees around the exposed annular body.
Extend from radius 58 mm to 70 mm behind the upper static lip using a cosine-eased cam transition.
Hold radius 70 mm with the full moon presented outside the mouth before the next swallow.

cycle.reset: There is no separate reset: the closed cam returns the slider every revolution. Reverse cranking is mechanically intended to be safe but tells the story backward.

interaction.invitation: A molded counterclockwise arrow at the grip and the moon paused in the open C-mouth tell the user what to turn and what to watch.
interaction.normal_use: Hold the base with one hand and turn the rounded grip counterclockwise slowly. Two crank turns produce one swallow-orbit-pop cycle; required hand torque and ergonomic comfort are unverified.
interaction.service: The central eye guard, front washer/key, moon, roller, crank, and lips are individually removable. The roller, grip, and slider are explicitly replaceable wear/failure parts.
interaction.spectacle: The user can see the gears, carrier rhythm, and moon path, while the fixed lips briefly occlude the radial translation; the mechanical cause and the creature story remain legible together.

mechanism_comparison.tradeoff: The moon is captive and positively driven inward and outward with no gravity reset. It produces continuous reversible motion and needs only one timing relationship, at the cost of a sliding dovetail, cam follower, and twenty-four printed pieces across twenty-two unique component types; eight of those pieces are simple flat washers or tapered retaining keys.

mechanism_comparison.architecture: Free-moon scoop wheel with gravity chute
mechanism_comparison.tradeoff: It would transfer a physically loose moon most literally, but cup/stripper clearance, rebound, orientation dependence, double feeds, jams, and a loose-part hazard make it substantially less robust.

It offers a dramatic staged gulp and release, but abrupt indexing, high tooth and drive-pin loads, a mistimed gate, more parts, and a stepped rather than flowing orbit weaken feasibility and the requested loop.

nominal_geometry_mm.declared_design_context: Targets assume a 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers, PLA or PETG, and a 200 x 200 mm bed; these are design assumptions, not verified printer or material results.

decisions: Mouth lips are stationary and conceal by axial overlap; no jaw closes on a finger.
Minimum exposed lip-to-moon clearance is 6 mm and all exposed edges receive at least 1.5 mm fillets.

Gear and cam planes are behind the moon plane; the fixed central eye guard overlaps the carrier gear, the crank-arm hub shield overlaps the pinion, and the frame rim blocks casual direct groove access.
There are no magnets, springs, stored-energy launchers, sharp points, loose free-running balls, or purchased parts.
The crank-arm grip post and replaceable grip are the intended low-strength overload region rather than a gear tooth, central axle, or frame fracture.
safety_design.unproven: These are design intentions only. Pinch accessibility, edge radii, breakaway behavior, retention, and age suitability require exact-geometry inspection and physical evidence in later authorized stages.

concept.summary: A support-free, all-printed desk automaton in which two hand-crank turns rotate a geared carrier once. A captive moon slider follows a fixed closed cam: it retracts behind a lower static lip as if swallowed, travels through a 286-degree exposed inner orbit around a one-eyed annular creature, then extends behind an upper lip and pauses outside the mouth before repeating. Static depth-overlap lips create the gulp/pop illusion without a closing-jaw pinch interface, and every load-bearing, guiding, retaining, and wearing element is printed and replaceable.
concept.title: Orbit Gobbler: C-Mouth Lunar Cam

unresolved_risks.required_make_evidence: Calculate peak dr/dtheta and pressure angle, run interference/motion checks, and lengthen transition arcs or reduce stroke if follower force is unacceptable while retaining a legible swallow/pop.
unresolved_risks.risk: The 12 mm radial stroke over each 30-degree cosine transition may still create excessive cam pressure angle, friction, or hand-torque ripple.

unresolved_risks.required_make_evidence: Render and inspect front plus 30-degree oblique views across the full transition; add stationary side cheeks only if they preserve at least 6 mm exposed clearance and remain support-free.
unresolved_risks.risk: The axial lip overlap may not conceal enough moon from oblique viewing angles.

unresolved_risks.required_make_evidence: Parameterize clearances, inspect STEP selectors and motion, and use fit coupons or physical samples before any performance claim.
unresolved_risks.risk: Dovetail friction, cam-wall friction, follower-axle/moon lug retention, and gear backlash depend on exact geometry and printer/material variation.

unresolved_risks.required_make_evidence: Compute mass properties from exact CAD and adjust the counterweight without infringing the cam or frame envelope.
unresolved_risks.risk: The provisional opposite counterweight may not adequately balance the moon, slider, and follower.

unresolved_risks.required_make_evidence: Inspect local minimum thickness and load direction, enlarge roots or change print orientation as needed, and do not claim durability without physical repeated-cycle evidence.
unresolved_risks.risk: Layer adhesion at the axle flange, crank post, moon stem, and roller peg may be insufficient.

unresolved_risks.required_make_evidence: Model insertion/removal paths and geometric capture, add a non-flexing detent or keeper if required, and physically verify retention before release.
unresolved_risks.risk: The transverse axle key and other keyed insertions may release unexpectedly, jam, or become non-serviceable.

wish_specific_identity.motion: The moon itself moves inward to be swallowed, remains visibly captive while orbiting the creature, and moves outward to pop back through the mouth; the mechanism is not a stock gear train hidden behind decoration.
wish_specific_identity.object: A cheerful but mechanically assertive one-eyed space creature whose annular body is the orbital stage and whose upper-right C-shaped mouth interrupts that orbit.
wish_specific_identity.resting_silhouette: Broad stable base, round ribbed creature body, single central eye, two asymmetric crescent lips, visible cratered moon, and a front crank grip that reads from across a desk.
wish_specific_identity.surface_language: Large rounded ribs, sparse star pits, one concentric eye, shallow moon craters, and exposed carrier motion; no color is required for comprehension.

design_decision_boundary.required_follow_up: Make must produce exact geometry and run deterministic layout, thickness, fit, mesh, and motion inspection. Any physical-print, cycle-life, friction, safety, or user-response claim requires later physical evidence and is not established by this Invent proposal.
design_decision_boundary.statement: All dimensions, clearances, angles, material examples, and manufacturing settings in the concept are deliberate starting decisions authored for Make, not externally verified universal facts.

supports: A Wish-specific printable kinetic machine with orbiting, revealing, and transforming motion is Bob's exact specialization.
Exposed cause and effect, parametric STEP-first parts, generous tolerances, serviceable wear parts, and explicit evidence boundaries are selected Taste requirements.
The design must avoid bought hardware, hidden supports, brittle pins, exposed stored energy, and performance claims without exact evidence.
Invent explored distinct motion architectures before selecting one spectacle.
The selected concept records the intended cycle, load path, reset, hazards, assumptions, envelope, wall thickness, component dimensions, placement, interfaces, assembly, and unresolved evidence gaps.
Comparison of closed-cam, loose-moon scoop, and Geneva architectures.
Selection and dimensional specification of the closed-groove radial-cam carrier with static axial-overlap lips.
Identification of cam slope, oblique concealment, friction, balance, layer adhesion, and retention as unresolved Make-stage risks.
This is a Forge Invent attempt with Bob selected only from the exact nine-entry host roster.
The concept must remain within the universal toy blueprint and defer unverified printability, mechanical performance, and physical response claims.
The product must be a support-free, all-printable hand-cranked desk automaton named Orbit Gobbler.
The required narrative cycle is swallow a moon, carry it through a clearly visible orbit, and pop it back out.
